metadata.title: ANT Stock Slips Below IPO Price In Premarket — Canaccord Sees Bigger AI Opportunity, 60% Upside Potential

content.text:
ANT Stock Slips Below IPO Price In Premarket — Canaccord Sees Bigger AI Opportunity, 60% Upside Potential
-
Canaccord said Anthropic is building one of the most important enterprise technology franchises of the AI era.
-
Oppenheimer initiated coverage of Anthropic with an 'Outperform' rating and a $150 price target.
-
Wedbush initiated coverage with an 'Outperform' rating and a $120 price target, calling Anthropic a leader in frontier AI models.
Anthropic (ANT) shares fell below their $83 initial public offering (IPO) price in Tuesday's premarket session, extending a sharp reversal just days after the Claude developer completed the largest IPO on record.
ANT stock dropped more than 6% to around $82, putting it nearly 29% below its debut-day high of $115.10.
Anthropic joins other major tech IPOs that fell below their offer prices. SpaceX (SPCX) took about a month, while Facebook, now Meta (META), slipped below its IPO price on its second trading day in 2012.
Anthropic's Record IPO Rally Unravels
Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq on November 19 at $111.50, a 34% premium to its $83 offering price. The shares briefly pushed the company's fully diluted valuation above $2 trillion before closing their first session at $97.17.
The stock fell to $87.64 at Monday's close, just 5.6% above its IPO price, even as the broader AI sector rebounded after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.
Meanwhile, regulatory filings on Monday showed that CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei each sold approximately $280.4 million worth of shares at the IPO price as part of the offering.
Canaccord Sees Opportunity Beyond Software Spending
Despite the stock's recent decline, Canaccord initiated coverage of Anthropic with a 'Buy' rating and a $135 price target, implying a nearly 65% upside from Tuesday's $82 premarket level.
The firm said Anthropic is building one of the most important enterprise technology franchises of the AI era, according to the note cited by TheFly. Canaccord said it is "increasingly convinced" that AI's potential market extends considerably beyond traditional software spending.
As AI evolves from helping employees perform tasks to completing the work itself, the firm expects the addressable market to expand into labor and broader operating budgets. Canaccord also considers Anthropic one of the industry's established leaders.
Oppenheimer also initiated coverage of Anthropic with an 'Outperform' rating and a $150 price target, citing its leadership in frontier AI models, rising enterprise adoption and improving compute efficiency. The firm sees a "substantial runway" within a $5.3 trillion commercial opportunity by 2030, forecasting $275.1 billion in revenue and operating margins above 20% in 2028.
